body_markdown:
Choosing a Christmas menu is easier when you start with how your group likes to eat. Some families want a familiar roast with dishes passed round the table. Others would love a slower meal with individual courses. Decide that first, then talk food with your chef.


To get you started, here are three real festive menus from yhangry chefs: a traditional Christmas lunch, a showstopper that isn’t turkey, and a fully plant-based feast. Each one comes from a chef who’s cooking with yhangry right now, and real prices from their bookings. Your own menu, price and availability will be agreed with your chef for your date.


## A traditional Christmas lunch


If the roast is the main event, leave room for it. A lighter starter makes more sense than a rich first course followed by a full plate of turkey and trimmings. Ask your chef which parts they’ll bring to the table to share and which they’ll plate.


Agree the details people care about most: the gravy, the stuffing, the roast potatoes and the vegetables. If some guests need different versions, talk through how those will be made and labelled, so a vegetarian guest knows exactly which shared sides are theirs.


### From the menu:[Chef Franck L](https://yhangry.com/booking/chef/franck-l/)


Last Christmas Day, Franck cooked for a family of 18 at their home in Essex. The menu let them build their own lunch from a long list:


Many of Franck’s dishes can be made vegan or allium-free, and he marks which ones on the menu. That mattered for this family: one guest couldn’t eat onion or garlic, and they said he made every guest feel thoughtfully catered for and left them free to relax with the family.


**What they paid:** £1,872 for 18 guests on 25 December 2025, about £104 a head, all in.


## A different festive centrepiece


Christmas dinner doesn’t have to be turkey. Beef Wellington, a whole fish or a rich vegetable pie can give the day a different feel. Ask your chef how the centrepiece is prepared and served, because a dish that needs precise last-minute finishing may change the timings or need an extra pair of hands.


Think about how adventurous your group wants to be. One unexpected course makes dinner exciting without asking every guest to navigate a menu of surprises. Tell your chef which familiar flavours you’d like to keep.


### From the menu:[Chef Vijayen M](https://yhangry.com/booking/chef/vijayen-m/)


Last Christmas Day, Vijayen and his assistant cooked a restaurant-style lunch for a family of 16 in Surrey. Their menu let guests choose three mains, so the table could share a mix of centrepieces:


The family said the food was beautifully presented and truly high-end, and that Vijayen and his assistant made a big Christmas service feel calm and effortless.


**What they paid:** £3,510 for 16 guests on 25 December 2025, about £219 a head, all in, including a second pair of hands in the kitchen.


## A plant-based festive feast


A plant-based Christmas can be a complete feast in its own right, not a plate of sides. Talk to your chef about texture, richness and portions so the centrepiece feels as special as any roast. They’ll suggest a main and trimmings that work together.


If you’re choosing plant-based because of an allergy rather than preference, say so clearly. Plant-based dishes can still contain nuts, wheat or soya, so agree what’s safe directly with your chef rather than relying on a menu label.


### From the menu:[Chef Tim B](https://yhangry.com/booking/chef/Tim-B/)


Tim’s vegan Christmas sharing menu is built for families who want a proper festive spread, with every dish made without animal products. He suggests picking two hot mains, two sides and a dessert:


That’s a good example of why allergies need a direct conversation: many of these dishes use nuts. Tim has a perfect five-star rating from his yhangry reviews, which often mention how carefully he handles allergies and dietary needs.

**Price:** quoted for your date and group. Tim’s recent dinner bookings have typically come to £60 to £90 a head, and Christmas Day is usually priced higher than other dates.


## Choose with the whole table in mind


Once you’ve picked a direction, check children’s meals, portion sizes and any separate dishes for dietary needs. Confirm whether canapés, a cheese board or extra desserts are included or optional. Sharing the final menu with guests in advance is a great way to surface questions while there’s still time to sort them.


All three menus above work the same way: the chef offers a list, and you choose the dishes that suit your group. That’s how many yhangry chefs build a Christmas menu, so you can mix the traditional with something new.


**Ready to plan yours?**[Tell us your date and postcode](https://yhangry.com/) and you’ll get festive menus and quotes from chefs near you. Mention which of these styles appeals and what you’d like to change.


FAQs


Can a private chef cook a traditional turkey dinner?


Yes. Many yhangry chefs offer a full turkey lunch with all the trimmings, often alongside beef, fish or vegetarian mains so you can mix and match.


What can we have instead of turkey for Christmas dinner?


Popular choices on yhangry menus include beef Wellington, slow-roasted beef rib, rack of lamb, halibut or salmon, and vegetarian showstoppers like a mushroom and chestnut pithivier or beetroot Wellington.


Can a private chef do a fully vegan Christmas dinner?


Yes. Some chefs offer complete vegan Christmas menus, with mains like nut roast, celeriac or chestnut pie and all the trimmings. If anyone has an allergy, talk it through with your chef directly.


How much does a Christmas menu from a private chef cost?


It depends on the date, your group size and the menu. Last Christmas Day, the menus in this guide came to between about £104 and £219 a head, all in.
